release 3.4 · candidate two

Prepare the account migration

Review the rollout plan, settle the remaining evidence question, and work through the migration queue without leaving this page.

Rollout plan

Move active accounts in three cohorts. Each cohort starts after the prior cohort has completed a full business day with matching account totals, successful sign-ins, and no increase in support contacts.

The migration copies account settings before switching reads. Writes continue to the current store until verification finishes, so returning a cohort does not require reconstructing reader changes.

Stages

  1. Internal accounts. Migrate staff and test tenants, compare settings and permissions, then hold for one business day.
  2. Ten percent. Select accounts across regions and plan types, then compare sign-in and settings-save rates with the control.
  3. Remaining accounts. Advance in four equal batches while the old store remains writable for rollback.

Advancement gates

Account totals
Exact match between stores
Successful sign-ins
No decrease greater than 0.2 percentage points
Settings saves
No increase in failed writes
Support contacts
No migration-related cluster

The evidence behind these gates and the one unresolved choice are in Evidence. The working list for individual cohorts is in the Workbench.

Rollback

A failed gate returns reads to the current store and stops later cohorts. The migration record keeps the copied rows and comparison output so the team can diagnose the mismatch before retrying.

The old store remains the write authority until all cohorts complete the observation period. Retiring it is a later release with its own plan.

Rehearsal results

Three rehearsals copied 48,219 accounts from a production snapshot. Every account and permission row matched after normalization, and all sampled accounts could sign in and save settings through the candidate service.

North America 18,104 21 minutes 0
Europe 16,780 19 minutes 0
Asia Pacific 13,335 17 minutes 0

Sign-in checks

The test covered password, passkey, and enterprise sign-in for new and long-lived sessions. Expired sessions refreshed once and returned to the requested page. Revoked sessions returned to sign-in without retrying.

  • 2,400 password sign-ins completed successfully.
  • 600 passkey sign-ins completed successfully.
  • 300 enterprise sign-ins completed successfully.
  • 120 expired sessions refreshed without duplicate requests.

How long should each cohort remain under observation?

Every rehearsal stabilized within four hours. A full business day also includes the daily permissions sync and the regional support handoff.

Four hours The rollout can finish in one day, before the daily permissions sync runs. One business day Each cohort includes the permissions sync and one support handoff before the next begins.

Follow-through

After settling the observation window, return to the rollout plan to confirm the schedule or open the Workbench queue to assign the first cohort.

How the comparison was performed

The verifier compared normalized account settings, permission rows, and tenant memberships by stable account id. It then replayed sign-in and settings-save journeys against the copied records.

Before migration

  • Capture account and permission totals by region.
  • Confirm the rollback writer is healthy.
  • Notify support of the cohort start and observation window.
  • Record the current sign-in and settings-save rates.

After migration

  • Compare copied account, tenant, and permission rows.
  • Run password, passkey, and enterprise sign-in checks.
  • Run the daily permissions sync against migrated accounts.
  • Review migration-related support contacts.
  • Record the advancement decision with its evidence.
